prompt: Write a note to a friend about a funny thing that happened with a neighbor. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Hey Sam,

You will not believe what happened with Dennis next door this week. I have to tell you while it's fresh.

So you know how he's been obsessed with his lawn since spring? He's out there at dawn with a tape measure, basically. Well, on Tuesday night I hear this scratching noise outside my kitchen window. I look out and there's Dennis, in the dark, wearing a headlamp, crouched over the strip of grass between our driveways. He's carefully pushing a little flag into the ground.

I opened the window and said, "Everything okay?" He nearly jumped out of his shoes. Turns out he'd had a surveyor come out that afternoon because he was convinced I'd been "creeping" my side of the property line over with my mulch bed. He was marking where the line really is so he could confront me with evidence.

And here's the thing. The surveyor's flags showed that the line is about eight inches *into his yard* from where he thought it was. Meaning HE has been mowing eight inches of MY lawn every week for three years. I did not have the heart to say that I'd noticed. Okay, I did, and I had the heart, but I let him have his moment.

So I stood there in my pajamas, and he stood there in his headlamp, and we both stared at the flags for a good while. Then he cleared his throat and said, very seriously, "Well. I suppose I owe you some grass."

I said I'd accept payment in the form of him continuing to mow it, since he does such a nice job. He laughed way harder than I expected. Then he went inside and came back with two beers, and we sat on my porch steps at ten at night, drinking and admiring the little orange flags.

Yesterday I came home and found a tiny hand-lettered sign stuck by the mulch bed. It said, "Property of Marcus. Dennis mows it."

I've decided to keep it up. It's the best thing anyone has ever done for me.

Anyway, come visit soon. I'll make Dennis give you the tour of the lawn. Bring a tape measure for the full effect.

Talk soon,
Marcus
